_about: Approved by Nav on 2026-11-20 (E0, prompts 43–44). The Grand Tour: stops, branches, distances, probes and their upgrade names, planet tech and cosmetics. Nothing reads this file yet; 8c and the E phases will. Upgrade effects and prices stay as in shared/upgrades.ts: only names and flavour lines change per probe. The planet tech here is smaller than the design's and credits-only, so it never changes trip speed (docs/expansion.md, 'Planet tech'). Distances are the gap between average distances from the Sun (or a moon's distance from its planet), from distanceSources; TODO marks what isn't checked.

sun.label: NASA NSSDC planetary fact sheet, distance from the Sun (million km): Mars 228.0, Jupiter 778.5, Saturn 1432.0, Uranus 2867.0, Neptune 4515.0, Pluto 5906.4

ceres.label: JPL Small-Body Database: Ceres a = 2.77 au

vesta.label: JPL Small-Body Database: Vesta a = 2.36 au

arrokoth.label: JPL Small-Body Database: Arrokoth a = 44.1 au

jovian.label: NASA NSSDC Jovian satellites (thousand km): Europa 671.1, Ganymede 1070.4

saturnian.label: NASA NSSDC Saturnian satellites (thousand km): Titan 1,221.87, Enceladus 238.02

uranian.label: NASA NSSDC Uranian satellites (thousand km): Miranda 129.90, Titania 436.30

fact.text: Every planet except Earth was named after Greek and Roman gods and goddesses.
fact.quote: All of the planets, except for Earth, were named after Greek and Roman gods and goddesses.

stops.name: Mars
stops.distanceNote: The game's route since phase 4 (the probe's travel path, as the design has it), not the gap in distance from the Sun (about 78M km).

tech.what: Offline cap for the whole crew, forever

fact.text: Ceres is the biggest object in the asteroid belt, and the only dwarf planet in the inner Solar System.
fact.quote: Dwarf planet Ceres is the largest object in the asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter.

tech.name: Vesta ore smelter
tech.what: Upgrade prices for the whole crew, forever

fact.text: Vesta is the second most massive body in the main asteroid belt, after Ceres.
fact.quote: the second most massive body in the main asteroid belt

tech.name: Gravity slingshot
tech.what: Credits from auto-thrust, for the whole crew, forever

fact.text: Jupiter is more than twice as massive as all the other planets put together.
fact.quote: more than twice as massive as the other planets combined

fact.text: Europa's hidden ocean may hold twice as much water as all of Earth's oceans.
fact.quote: its ocean may contain twice as much water as Earth's global ocean

tech.name: Magnetic shield
tech.what: Auto-thrust credits keep paying in safe mode
tech.note: Replaces the design's 'safe-mode setback halved', which would change trip speed.

fact.text: Ganymede is the biggest moon in the Solar System, even bigger than the planet Mercury.
fact.quote: the largest moon in our solar system, even bigger than the planet Mercury

stops.name: Saturn
stops.distanceNote: From Jupiter's distance from the Sun; the moon legs before it are tiny next to this.

fact.text: Saturn is the only planet whose average density is less than water's.
fact.quote: Saturn is the only planet in our solar system with an average density that is less than water.

fact.text: Titan is the only moon with a thick atmosphere, and it has seas of liquid methane and ethane.
fact.quote: It is the only moon with a thick atmosphere. ... liquid hydrocarbons like methane and ethane

fact.text: Jets on Enceladus spray water vapour and ice into space, and the spray forms Saturn's E ring.
fact.quote: geyser-like jets spewing water vapor and ice particles into space ... to form Saturn's E ring

fact.text: Uranus spins at nearly 90 degrees to its orbit, so it rolls around the Sun on its side.
fact.quote: Uranus rotates at a nearly 90-degree angle from the plane of its orbit.

fact.text: Miranda's giant canyons are up to 12 times as deep as the Grand Canyon.
fact.quote: Miranda's giant fault canyons are as much as 12 times as deep as the Grand Canyon.

tech.name: Fairy lights
tech.what: Credits from taps between midnight and 6 am, your local time
tech.note: The design says 00:00 to 06:00 UTC; local time matches the Night Shift badge.

fact.text: Titania, Uranus's biggest moon, is named after the queen of the fairies in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream.
fact.quote: Titania is named for the queen of the fairies in William Shakespeare's 16th century play

fact.text: Neptune is the windiest world in the Solar System, with winds over 2,000 km/h.
fact.quote: speeds of more than 1,200 miles per hour (2,000 kilometers per hour)

fact.text: Pluto's biggest plains seem to be made of frozen nitrogen, with no craters at all.
fact.quote: The most prominent plains observed on Pluto appear to be made of frozen nitrogen gas and show no craters.

fact.text: NASA's New Horizons flew past Arrokoth, far out in the Kuiper belt, on 1 January 2019.
fact.quote: On Jan. 1, 2019, the spacecraft flew by a Kuiper Belt object later named Arrokoth.

stops.name: Heliopause
stops.distanceNote: TODO: no NASA page read on 2026-11-20 gives the heliopause's distance from the Sun. The design's ~11B km from the Kuiper belt is unchecked.

fact.text: On 25 August 2012, Voyager 1 became the first spacecraft to leave the Sun's bubble, the heliosphere.
fact.quote: On Aug. 25, 2012, the spacecraft became the first to exit the heliosphere

stops.name: Interstellar space
stops.distanceNote: Endless: distance records and monthly trophies instead of an arrival (docs/expansion.md).

fact.text: Voyager 1 is the first human-made object to travel into interstellar space.
fact.quote: Voyager 1 is the first human-made object to venture into interstellar space.
